circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281-kilometre facility designed by Hermann Tilke on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue following Bahrain, with Qatar and Saudi Arabia later joining the regional calendar.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling a lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various supporting racing categories. The venue holds the highest FIA safety classification.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit originated as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following a redesign and renaming in the 1990s, the track resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street circuit in Azerbaijan's capital that spans 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest track in Formula One. It first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Inaugurated in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosts the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, marking the championship's debut in the Middle East. The venue accommodates various motorsports including GP2 racing, drag racing, and endurance competitions, while holding an FIA Grade 1 license with alternative track configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km facility represents a balanced test of racing machinery with its combination of extended straightaways and diverse corner sequences. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been hosting Formula One racing since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The venue has maintained its status as the home of the Belgian Grand Prix with remarkable consistency, running annually from 1985 onwards with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometer temporary street circuit that hosts the FIA Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its role as a premier single-seater venue, the track has also accommodated various other racing series including sportscar championships and North American open-wheel and stock-car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit is a Chinese motorsport venue located in Shanghai's Jiading district that gained prominence as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually between 2004 and 2019 before resuming in 2024. Beyond hosting the Formula One event, the facility began accommodating the Shanghai ePrix from 2024 onwards.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue situated near Northamptonshire that became the inaugural venue for the World Championship of Drivers in 1950. The track hosted the British Grand Prix from its inception in 1948, though the race alternated with two other circuits between 1955 and 1986 before returning permanently to Silverstone from 1987 onward. Beyond Formula One, the facility also stages major motorcycle racing events.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc when it debuted in 1986, chosen over a proposed street circuit in the city's main park. Built in just eight months starting from October 1985, the 4. 381 km permanent facility was constructed faster than any other Formula One circuit and inaugurated with its first race in March 1986 as a tribute to Hungarian motorcycle racing pioneer János Drapál.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located north of Milan in Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale di Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 and remains mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility. The venue hosts the Italian Grand Prix, a fixture on the Formula One calendar since 1949 with only a single interruption in 1980, and earns the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its distinctive long straights and fast-corner design.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka International Racing Course is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport facility operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track primarily hosts Formula One and Super Formula racing events at the highest competitive levels.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track located in Paradise, Nevada that follows roads through the famous Las Vegas Strip, home to major casino resorts and hotels. The layout passes by iconic Las Vegas landmarks such as the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it winds through the urban streets.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honors two racing brothers who died in motorsport accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The circuit has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix across multiple eras, with the current continuous run beginning in 2015 on its present layout, now officially titled the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that serves as the venue for the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022. The 3. 363-mile track comprises 19 corners and achieves average qualifying speeds of approximately 139 mph, having been designed by specialist firm Apex Circuit Design.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine in the Principality of Monaco, spanning 3. 337 kilometers around the harbor area. Though officially known as the Circuit de Monaco, it is widely called "Monte Carlo" due to its location primarily within that Monaco neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track known for its dramatic elevation changes and steeply banked corners that create a thrilling, undulating racing experience. The venue hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026, earning the nickname "The Roller Coaster in the Dunes" for its distinctive terrain winding through the North Sea dunes with signature turns like Tarzan and Hugenholtz.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Located north of Doha in Qatar, the Lusail International Circuit is a 5. 419 km track featuring a 1. 068 km main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace. The venue has hosted numerous Grand Prix events and features additional karting facilities dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah. Since its debut in 2021, it has served as the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, with Formula E racing also joining the calendar from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas. This temporary street track hosts the Formula One Grand Prix on Singapore's urban streets around the bay.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced mix of high-speed straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple racing skills. With FIA Grade 1 certification and seating for approximately 140,700 spectators, the venue serves as an all-purpose racing facility.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas near Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA circuit that serves as the venue for the United States Formula One Grand Prix alongside major motorsport events including MotoGP and sports car racing championships. The track has hosted a diverse range of international racing series throughout its history, from IndyCar to various endurance racing formats.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Thai-British driver Alexander Albon currently races for Williams in Formula One under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two World Championship titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond his top-tier racing achievements, Alonso has demonstrated versatility through success in endurance competition, notably winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and claiming two Le Mans 24-hour victories with Toyota, establishing himself as the sole driver to achieve championships across both Formula One and world sportscar racing.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli secured the 2026 Formula One championship with Mercedes at a record young age, adding nine race victories to his resume following his entry into the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas in the championship.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto competes in Formula One for Audi, bringing his racing expertise to the team's competitive efforts in the sport.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing over a decade of experience to the grid. His career highlights include two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his Mercedes tenure, along with 10 Grand Prix victories accumulated across his 13 seasons in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, serves as a reserve driver for Haas in Formula One while competing in endurance racing. He has participated in seven Formula One Grands Prix between 2024 and 2025, and currently races in the LMP2 category of the Asian Le Mans Series with AF Corse following previous stints in European Le Mans competition.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One competitor currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix during his tenure with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One competition, driving for Red Bull Racing, while holding dual French and Algerian citizenship.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: British driver Lewis Hamilton competes for Ferrari in Formula One, where he has secured seven world championship titles, equaling Michael Schumacher's record. He holds the sport's most victories with 106 wins, alongside leading records for pole positions and podium appearances.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One and has demonstrated significant success beyond the sport's premier category, notably claiming victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc represents Ferrari on the Formula One grid as a Monégasque driver, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career. He achieved his strongest championship finish in 2022 when he finished as runner-up in the drivers' standings.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who previously competed in Formula One across two separate periods, most recently concluding in 2024. He currently focuses his racing efforts on the FIA World Endurance Championship, representing BMW as a factory driver for WRT, while also undertaking selected NASCAR Cup Series appearances for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, became Formula One World Champion in 2025 after claiming 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The driver previously secured a notable victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican driver competing for Cadillac in Formula One, finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while representing Red Bull. Over his 15-season career in the sport, he has claimed victory in six Grand Prix events.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his four-year tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: The Australian driver competed in Formula One throughout a 14-year career spanning 2011 to 2024, claiming victory in eight races during his time in the sport. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", Ricciardo has since retired from top-level racing.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Mercedes who has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories over the course of his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons. He currently competes in the World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously participated in IMSA's LMP2 class with Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Canadian driver Lance Stroll currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, competing at the sport's highest level.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, held a full-time Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing, having secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, he has accumulated 74 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is the sole Chinese competitor to have raced in Formula One, participating in the championship from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in the series.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based operation has competed as Alpine since 2021, carrying the name of Renault's performance vehicle marque while maintaining works team status for the French manufacturer. Previously racing under the Renault banner, the squad transitioned to Alpine branding as part of Groupe Renault's strategic repositioning before the parent company's withdrawal from the championship at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has competed in Formula One across multiple incarnations, with the current outfit operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian luxury carmaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished competitor, having entered every World Championship season since the series began in 1950. Commonly called "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, the team remains the sport's oldest continuously active participant.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-based Formula One team founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, making its competitive debut in 2016 after establishment in 2014. Leadership recently transitioned when Ayao Komatsu assumed the team principal position following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, ending Steiner's tenure since the team's inception.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering outfit established in 1970, this independent constructor earned endurance racing laurels including the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours before joining Formula One in 1993. After three decades of competition and multiple transformations, the team concluded its racing operations in 2025 as the fourth most experienced constructor by race entries, with its operations subsequently acquired by Audi to serve as the foundation for their Formula One programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at their Woking facility, operating as a subsidiary within the wider McLaren Group and owned by Bahraini investment firm Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One continuously since 1954, operating as both a constructor and engine supplier across multiple eras. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas team, based in Brackley under a German licence, became a three-way partnership in 2022 when Ineos joined Mercedes-Benz and Toto Wolff as equal stakeholders. The team's identity is traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" nomenclature.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as one of two constructors under Red Bull GmbH's ownership. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister operation to Red Bull Racing within the Red Bull motorsport portfolio.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced competition in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull GmbH-affiliated squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team represents the Austrian conglomerate's second constructor entry into the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team based in England that has been part of Red Bull GmbH's motorsport portfolio since 2005. Under Christian Horner's leadership from inception until 2025, the team established itself as a competitive force in the championship, with Laurent Mekies taking over as team principal following Horner's departure. Red Bull GmbH also operates a second Formula One entry through Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British constructor founded by Frank Williams and Patrick Head in 1977, represents the continuation of Williams's earlier failed F1 venture. Currently competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team, the squad operates from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters and has established itself as a significant force in Formula One's technical and competitive landscape.
